promptAsSent:
Use the image_gen tool to generate exactly one image, then stop. Do not write files, run commands or edit anything.

Attached reference images, in order:
Image 1: Geometry/layout authority: the edit target
Image 2: Material/style only; not layout

Asset type: production-source concept master for a top-down game sprite: the chassis of a new Tri-Tachyon HIGH-TECH mech line, a heavy lance platform walking machine: a wide flux shield and a shoulder-mounted lance laser, drawn in the same design language as Starsector's high-tech warships.

Image 1 is the exact silhouette and layout authority, a grey value blockout: fill it in, never move, resize or add to its shapes, and keep all empty canvas empty, including the open channel between the two nose lobes where a gun barrel shows. It is built as separate armour lobes with wide channels of exposed machinery between them. The grey values mean: the DARK shapes are the exposed machine core, a dense mass of dark gunmetal machinery (ribbed conduits, actuator stacks, heat-sink fins, cable bundles, small blue-lit ports) that shows in every gap between the lobes and as a ribbed engine bank at the rear; the MID-GREY smooth shapes are armour lobes, each one a bulging, rounded shell with soft highlights and deep shading at its edges, like carapace; the light flat rectangle on the spine is a plain mounting plate where a weapon pod bolts on later; the small light disc near the front is a sensor bulb; the lightest disc is the SHIELD EMITTER, a round projector bulb with a soft blue core. The dark rings set into the shoulder lobes are recessed round weapon sockets, empty. Symmetric about the vertical centre line.

Image 2 is material and style reference only, never layout: Starsector's high-tech hulls, the Tempest, Aurora, Medusa and Paragon. Match their finish: pale steel-blue and blue-grey armour shells with cool blue shading, rounded and layered, set over dark, busy, finely detailed machinery; round recessed weapon mounts sunk into the shells; small blue glow slots; a little wear, scorch and grime in the recesses; light from the upper left. Paint it at full resolution as a crisp, detailed game-sprite master, not pixel art.

Strict 90-degree zenith orthographic top-down view of the chassis top surfaces, the machine facing the TOP edge of the canvas. True transparent background, including all negative space; no ground, shadow slab, cast shadow, halo, glow outside the machine, border, text, labels or logos. Draw only the chassis body: no weapons, missile racks, drones, legs or feet, which are separate layers drawn later.

Avoid: clean white plastic, flat untextured panels, long glowing light strips, rivets, tan or olive paint, a framed canopy, a pilot figure, perspective, side view, isometric view, cropped edges, a second machine, text.
agentMessages: I’ll use the image-generation tool to fill the exact blockout with the referenced high-tech materials and preserve the transparent negative space.
